name: Technology & Computing
description: Test your knowledge on computers, algorithms, the internet, and gadgets across 11 levels.

questions.question: Who is widely regarded as the father of modern theoretical computer science and AI?
questions.explanation: Alan Turing formalized concepts of computation with the Turing Machine and contributed to cryptanalysis at Bletchley Park.

questions.question: What does 'HTTP' stand for in web network communications?
questions.explanation: HTTP is the foundational application protocol used for fetching web documents over the internet.

questions.question: Which programming language was developed by Google and powers the Flutter framework?
questions.explanation: Dart is an object-oriented, client-optimized language created by Google for high-performance multi-platform apps.

questions.question: In what year was the first Apple iPhone officially introduced by Steve Jobs?
questions.explanation: Steve Jobs unveiled the original iPhone at Macworld in San Francisco on January 9, 2007.

questions.question: What does the acronym 'GPU' stand for in computing hardware?
questions.explanation: A GPU is a specialized electronic circuit designed to rapidly manipulate and alter memory to accelerate graphics rendering and parallel compute.

questions.question: What is the primary volatile memory used by a computer to hold data actively being processed?
questions.explanation: RAM (Random Access Memory) provides high-speed read/write access to instructions and data currently in use.

questions.question: What binary digits are used to represent all digital information in computers?
questions.explanation: Binary notation uses combinations of 0s and 1s representing electrical off/on states.

questions.question: How many bits make up one standard byte?
questions.explanation: One byte equals eight binary digits (bits), capable of holding 256 distinct values.

questions.question: What is the fundamental purpose of an operating system (OS)?
options: Manage computer hardware and software resources
questions.explanation: An OS acts as an intermediary between users/applications and computer hardware.

questions.question: What does 'URL' stand for in web browsing?
questions.explanation: A URL specifies the address and protocol used to access a resource on the web.

questions.question: Who created the Python programming language in the late 1980s?
questions.explanation: Dutch programmer Guido van Rossum created Python, first released in 1991.

questions.question: Which programming language is compiled into bytecode that runs on the Java Virtual Machine (JVM)?
questions.explanation: Java source code compiles into platform-independent `.class` bytecode executed by the JVM.

questions.question: Who created the C programming language at Bell Laboratories in 1972?
questions.explanation: Dennis Ritchie developed C to re-implement the Unix operating system.

questions.question: What programming paradigm is centered on concepts such as classes, inheritance, and encapsulation?
questions.explanation: OOP organizes software design around data or objects, rather than functions and logic.

questions.question: What standard language is used for managing and querying data stored in relational databases?
questions.explanation: Structured Query Language (SQL) is the standard domain-specific language for relational database management.

questions.question: Which language was created in 10 days by Brendan Eich in 1995 for Netscape Navigator?
questions.explanation: Brendan Eich developed JavaScript (originally Mocha/LiveScript) in May 1995.

questions.question: What modern systems programming language created by Mozilla emphasizes memory safety without a garbage collector?
questions.explanation: Rust uses an ownership and borrow-checker model to guarantee memory safety at compile time.

questions.question: What does 'API' stand for in software engineering?
questions.explanation: An API defines rules and specifications that allow different software programs to communicate with each other.

questions.question: What data format uses key-value pairs and human-readable text derived from JavaScript object notation?
questions.explanation: JSON (JavaScript Object Notation) is the dominant data interchange format in modern web APIs.

questions.question: In software architecture, what does 'DRY' stand for?
questions.explanation: The DRY principle aims to reduce repetition of software patterns and logic.

questions.question: Who is celebrated as the inventor of the World Wide Web at CERN in 1989?
questions.explanation: Sir Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web, HTTP, HTML, and the first web browser.

questions.question: What system translates human-friendly domain names (like google.com) into numerical IP addresses?
questions.explanation: The Domain Name System (DNS) acts as the phonebook of the internet.

questions.question: What is the current standard format for IPv4 addresses?
questions.explanation: IPv4 uses 32-bit addresses written in dot-decimal notation, allowing ~4.3 billion unique IPs.

questions.question: How many bits are used in an IPv6 address?
questions.explanation: IPv6 uses 128-bit addresses, providing an exponentially larger pool of 3.4 x 10^38 unique addresses.

questions.question: What secure protocol encrypts communication between a web browser and a website?
questions.explanation: HTTPS uses Transport Layer Security (TLS/SSL) to encrypt web traffic against eavesdropping.

questions.question: What device directs network data packets between different computer networks?
questions.explanation: A router inspects destination IP addresses and forwards packets between networks.

questions.question: What technology allows electronic devices to connect to a wireless local area network using radio waves?
questions.explanation: Wi-Fi is based on the IEEE 802.11 family of standards for wireless local networking.

questions.question: What port number is standard for non-encrypted HTTP web traffic?
questions.explanation: Port 80 is the default TCP port for HTTP; Port 443 is used for secure HTTPS.

questions.question: What protocol is used for securely logging into and managing remote servers via a command-line terminal?
questions.explanation: Secure Shell (SSH) provides cryptographic network protocol for remote terminal operations.

questions.question: What does 'LAN' stand for in computer networking?
questions.explanation: A LAN connects computers within a limited geographic area like a home, office, or school building.

questions.question: What component is often called the 'brain' of a computer system?
questions.explanation: The CPU executes the instructions of computer programs and performs arithmetic and logic.

questions.question: What empirical observation stated that the number of transistors on a microchip doubles roughly every two years?
questions.explanation: Formulated by Intel co-founder Gordon Moore in 1965, Moore's Law guided semiconductor scaling for decades.

questions.question: What microscopic semiconductor device acts as an electronic switch and amplifier in computer chips?
questions.explanation: Transistors are the building blocks of modern microprocessors and memory chips.

questions.question: Which computer memory is non-volatile and permanently contains startup instructions (BIOS/UEFI)?
questions.explanation: ROM (Read-Only Memory) retains its stored contents even when the computer is turned off.

questions.question: What modern solid-state storage device uses flash memory instead of spinning magnetic platters?
questions.explanation: Solid State Drives (SSDs) offer significantly faster read/write speeds and greater shock resistance than mechanical HDDs.

questions.question: What is the main printed circuit board connecting CPU, memory, and peripheral components?
questions.explanation: The motherboard (system board) provides communication pathways (buses) between hardware components.

questions.question: What type of ultrafast memory is built directly into the CPU chip to reduce latency?
questions.explanation: SRAM cache (L1, L2, L3) sits directly on the CPU die to store frequently accessed data.

questions.question: What interface standard is widely used to connect peripherals like keyboards, mice, and flash drives?
questions.explanation: Universal Serial Bus (USB) is the universal industry standard for digital peripherals.

questions.question: What does 'clock speed' of a modern CPU measure?
options: The number of cycles the CPU executes per second
questions.explanation: Clock speed (measured in gigahertz, GHz) reflects the frequency of CPU instruction cycles.

questions.question: Which company designed the x86 microprocessor architecture that dominates personal computers?
questions.explanation: Intel introduced the x86 architecture with the 8086 processor in 1978.

questions.question: Who created the open-source Linux kernel in 1991 while a university student in Helsinki?
questions.explanation: Linus Torvalds announced Linux as a free operating system kernel for 386 computers in 1991.

questions.question: What operating system created by Bell Labs in the 1960s inspired Linux and macOS?
questions.explanation: Unix established core concepts like the hierarchical file system and modular command-line utilities.

questions.question: What open-source operating system developed by Google powers billions of smartphones globally?
questions.explanation: Android is an open-source mobile OS based on a modified version of the Linux kernel.

questions.question: Which operating system developed by Microsoft introduced the iconic 'Start' button in 1995?
questions.explanation: Windows 95 introduced the Start menu, taskbar, and integrated 32-bit architecture.

questions.question: What is the core of an operating system that maintains complete control over the entire system?
questions.explanation: The kernel manages system resources, process scheduling, memory allocation, and hardware communication.

questions.question: What text-based interface allows users to communicate with the OS by typing commands?
questions.explanation: A CLI (such as bash, zsh, or PowerShell) interprets typed commands to perform operations.

questions.question: What open-source project founded by Richard Stallman in 1983 created free software tools for Unix-like systems?
questions.explanation: GNU ('GNU's Not Unix') provided the compilers, libraries, and utilities that pair with Linux.

questions.question: What Unix-based core foundation powers Apple's macOS and iOS?
questions.explanation: Darwin is the open-source POSIX-compliant Unix operating system base of macOS and iOS.

questions.question: What is the mechanism by which an OS temporarily stores inactive RAM data on the hard drive?
questions.explanation: Virtual memory moves memory pages to disk (swap space) when physical RAM is exhausted.

questions.question: What is the file system format natively used by modern Microsoft Windows operating systems?
questions.explanation: New Technology File System (NTFS) provides journaling, permissions, and file compression.

questions.question: What open-source UI toolkit was launched by Google in 2017 to build natively compiled apps from a single codebase?
questions.explanation: Flutter compiles Dart code into native ARM/x64 machine code for iOS, Android, web, and desktop.

questions.question: What is the official programming language recommended by Apple for building iOS and macOS apps since 2014?
questions.explanation: Apple introduced Swift at WWDC 2014 to replace Objective-C with modern safety and syntax.

questions.question: What modern language was announced by Google in 2017 as the preferred language for Android development?
questions.explanation: Kotlin, developed by JetBrains, offers conciseness, null-safety, and interoperability with Java.

questions.question: What file extension is used for compiled Android application package files?
questions.explanation: An Android Package Kit (APK) is the package file format used by Android to distribute and install apps.

questions.question: What file format is used for iOS application archive bundles ready for installation?
questions.explanation: An iOS App Store Package (.ipa) file is an iOS application archive.

questions.question: In Flutter, what fundamental concept represents almost everything in the user interface?
questions.explanation: In Flutter, 'everything is a widget'—from layout models (Padding, Row) to structural elements (Scaffold, Text).

questions.question: What cross-platform mobile framework developed by Meta (Facebook) uses JavaScript and React?
questions.explanation: React Native allows developers to build mobile apps using React and native platform UI primitives.

questions.question: What package manager is standard for managing Dart and Flutter workspace packages?
questions.explanation: The `pub` package manager and `pub.dev` repository host community libraries for Dart and Flutter.

questions.question: What Flutter tool allows developers to view code changes instantly without restarting the app state?
questions.explanation: Stateful Hot Reload injects updated source code into the running Dart VM in under a second.

questions.question: What tool is the official integrated development environment (IDE) for Android development by Google?
questions.explanation: Android Studio is based on JetBrains IntelliJ IDEA software and configured specifically for Android.

questions.question: What markup language provides the fundamental structure and content for all World Wide Web documents?
questions.explanation: HyperText Markup Language (HTML) defines headings, paragraphs, links, and document structure.

questions.question: What language is used for styling and visually formatting HTML web documents?
questions.explanation: Cascading Style Sheets (CSS) controls colors, fonts, layouts, and responsive design.

questions.question: Which cloud computing service platform was launched by Amazon in 2006, leading the cloud market?
questions.explanation: AWS launched S3 and EC2 in 2006, establishing the modern public cloud computing model.

questions.question: What version control system created by Linus Torvalds in 2005 is used by millions of developers?
questions.explanation: Git is a distributed version control system designed for speed and non-linear workflows.

questions.question: What popular web-based hosting platform for software development using Git was acquired by Microsoft in 2018?
questions.explanation: GitHub hosts hundreds of millions of public and private code repositories.

questions.question: What open-source containerization platform automates the deployment of apps in lightweight isolated packages?
questions.explanation: Docker packages applications and dependencies into standardized containers that run identically anywhere.

questions.question: What container orchestration system was originally designed by Google before being donated to CNCF?
questions.explanation: Kubernetes (K8s) automates deployment, scaling, and operational management of containerized workloads.

questions.question: What architectural style uses HTTP requests to GET, POST, PUT, and DELETE data over web APIs?
questions.explanation: Representational State Transfer (REST) leverages standard HTTP verbs and stateless communication.

questions.question: What does 'SaaS' stand for in cloud service models?
questions.explanation: Software as a Service delivers software applications over the internet on a subscription basis.

questions.question: What JavaScript runtime environment built on Chrome's V8 engine enables running JS on servers?
questions.explanation: Ryan Dahl created Node.js in 2009, enabling scalable server-side JavaScript programming.

questions.question: What fraudulent practice involves tricking individuals into revealing passwords or credit card numbers via deceptive emails?
questions.explanation: Phishing attacks impersonate trustworthy entities to deceive victims into handing over sensitive credentials.

questions.question: What security barrier monitors and filters incoming and outgoing network traffic based on predetermined rules?
questions.explanation: A firewall establishes a barrier between a trusted internal network and untrusted external traffic.

questions.question: What type of malicious software encrypts a victim's files and demands payment for the decryption key?
questions.explanation: Ransomware attacks (such as WannaCry) hold files hostage until a ransom is paid.

questions.question: What asymmetric public-key cryptography algorithm is named after Rivest, Shamir, and Adleman?
questions.explanation: RSA was introduced in 1977 and relies on the practical difficulty of factoring large composite prime numbers.

questions.question: What authentication method requires two independent pieces of evidence before granting user access?
questions.explanation: 2FA combines something you know (password) with something you have (phone/token) or are (fingerprint).

questions.question: What cryptographic hash function designed by the NSA produces a 256-bit digest and is used in Bitcoin?
questions.explanation: SHA-256 (part of SHA-2) generates a unique fixed-length 32-byte hash from arbitrary data.

questions.question: What cyberattack floods a target web server or network with excessive traffic to make it unavailable?
questions.explanation: DDoS attacks weaponize networks of infected computers (botnets) to overwhelm victim bandwidth.

questions.question: What symmetric encryption standard with key sizes of 128, 192, and 256 bits is widely used globally today?
questions.explanation: AES was established by NIST in 2001 and protects government and commercial data worldwide.

questions.question: What term describes a software vulnerability that is actively exploited before the vendor has released a patch?
questions.explanation: A zero-day flaw gives developers 'zero days' to prepare a patch once discovery becomes public.

questions.question: What wireless security protocol standard introduced in 2018 succeeded WPA2 to secure Wi-Fi networks?
questions.explanation: WPA3 provides robust individualized data encryption and brute-force protection for Wi-Fi.

questions.question: What subfield of artificial intelligence focuses on algorithms that learn patterns from training data?
questions.explanation: Machine Learning algorithms build mathematical models from sample data to make predictions without explicit programming.

questions.question: What computational models inspired by the biological human brain power deep learning?
questions.explanation: Neural networks use interconnected layers of nodes (neurons) to process complex input data.

questions.question: What benchmark proposed in 1950 tests a machine's ability to exhibit intelligent behavior indistinguishable from a human?
questions.explanation: Alan Turing's 'Imitation Game' assesses whether a human judge can distinguish a machine from a person.

questions.question: What AI domain enables computers to understand, interpret, and generate human spoken and written languages?
questions.explanation: NLP combines linguistics and machine learning to analyze text and speech.

questions.question: What deep learning architecture introduced in the 2017 paper 'Attention Is All You Need' powers modern LLMs?
questions.explanation: The Transformer architecture uses self-attention mechanisms to process sequence data in parallel.

questions.question: Which company developed the generative AI model ChatGPT, launched in November 2022?
questions.explanation: OpenAI released ChatGPT, which reached 100 million monthly active users within two months.

questions.question: What AI program developed by Google DeepMind defeated 18-time world champion Lee Sedol at Go in 2016?
questions.explanation: AlphaGo's 4-1 victory in Seoul marked a historic milestone for artificial intelligence.

questions.question: What technique trains AI agents through a system of actions, states, rewards, and penalties?
questions.explanation: Reinforcement learning optimizes an agent's policy to maximize cumulative rewards over time.

questions.question: What open-source deep learning library was developed by Google Brain and released in 2015?
questions.explanation: TensorFlow provides a comprehensive ecosystem for building and deploying machine learning models.

questions.question: What deep learning AI system created by DeepMind predicted 3D protein structures with atomic accuracy in 2020?
questions.explanation: AlphaFold solved a 50-year-old grand challenge in biology by predicting protein folding.

questions.question: Who is recognized as the world's first computer programmer for writing an algorithm for the Analytical Engine in 1843?
questions.explanation: Ada Lovelace translated Menabrea's paper and appended an algorithm to compute Bernoulli numbers.

questions.question: Which American computer pioneer coined the term 'debugging' after finding an actual moth inside the Mark II computer?
questions.explanation: Rear Admiral Grace Hopper was a pioneer who developed the first compiler and influenced COBOL.

questions.question: Who co-founded Apple Computer alongside Steve Jobs in 1976 and single-handedly designed the Apple I and II?
questions.explanation: Steve Wozniak ('Woz') designed the hardware and circuit boards for Apple's first computers.

questions.question: Who co-founded Microsoft Corporation alongside Paul Allen in 1975?
questions.explanation: Bill Gates and Paul Allen founded Microsoft to develop and sell BASIC interpreters for the Altair 8800.

questions.question: Who founded Amazon.com in 1994 as an online bookstore operating out of his garage?
questions.explanation: Jeff Bezos started Amazon in Seattle, growing it into the world's largest online retail and cloud enterprise.

questions.question: Who co-founded Google while Ph.D. students at Stanford University in 1998?
questions.explanation: Larry Page and Sergey Brin developed the PageRank algorithm and incorporated Google in September 1998.

questions.question: Who founded the social networking service Facebook in his Harvard dormitory room in 2004?
questions.explanation: Mark Zuckerberg launched 'TheFacebook' in February 2004 for Harvard students.

questions.question: Who led the software engineering team at MIT that developed the on-board Apollo Guidance Computer flight software?
questions.explanation: Margaret Hamilton pioneered software engineering, ensuring the Apollo 11 lunar module could land safely.

questions.question: Who invented the modern computer mouse in 1964 and demonstrated it in the 'Mother of All Demos' in 1968?
questions.explanation: Douglas Engelbart at SRI demonstrated the mouse, hypertext, windows, and video conferencing in 1968.

questions.question: Who invented the relational database model while working at IBM in 1970?
questions.explanation: E.F. Codd published 'A Relational Model of Data for Large Shared Data Banks', founding modern database theory.

questions.question: What is the basic unit of information in quantum computing, capable of superposition?
questions.explanation: A quantum bit (qubit) can exist in superpositions of state |0⟩ and |1⟩ simultaneously.

questions.question: Who published the Bitcoin whitepaper under a pseudonym in October 2008?
questions.explanation: Satoshi Nakamoto published 'Bitcoin: A Peer-to-Peer Electronic Cash System', releasing the open-source software in 2009.

questions.question: What sensor technology uses pulsed laser light to measure distances and map 3D environments in self-driving cars?
questions.explanation: LiDAR (Light Detection and Ranging) generates precise 3D point cloud maps of surrounding environments.

questions.question: What technology overlays computer-generated visual content onto the real-world view?
questions.explanation: Augmented Reality (AR) enhances real environments with digital projections and overlays.

questions.question: What decentralized digital ledger records transactions across a network of computers tamper-resistantly?
questions.explanation: A blockchain groups transactions into cryptographically linked chronological blocks.

questions.question: What generation of cellular broadband technology began global deployment around 2019 offering gigabit speeds?
questions.explanation: 5G networks offer high multi-Gbps peak data speeds, ultra-low latency, and massive device connectivity.

questions.question: What self-executing contracts with the terms directly written into code run on Ethereum?
questions.explanation: Smart contracts automatically execute agreed-upon actions when predetermined conditions are verified.

questions.question: What computing paradigm processes data close to the source where it is generated rather than in a distant data center?
questions.explanation: Edge computing reduces bandwidth use and latency by computing on local gateways or IoT devices.

questions.question: What facial recognition technology introduced by Apple with iPhone X uses a dot projector and infrared camera?
questions.explanation: Face ID projects over 30,000 infrared dots to build a 3D depth map of the user's face.

questions.question: What term describes microscopic manipulation of matter on an atomic, molecular, and supramolecular scale?
questions.explanation: Nanotechnology operates at scales between 1 and 100 nanometers.
